title.zh: 卷九十 志第六十六 兵二
title.raw: 卷九十 志第六十六 兵二 Volume 90 Treatises 66: Military 2

sentences.zh: 衛所班軍

translations.literal: Guard posts, companies, and rotational troops
translations.idiomatic: Guard Posts, Companies, and Rotational Troops

sentences.zh: 太祖下集慶路為吳王，罷諸翼統軍元帥，置武德、龍驤、豹韜、飛熊、威武、廣武、興武、英武、鷹揚、驍騎、神武、雄武、鳳翔、天策、振武、宣武、羽林十七衛親軍指揮使司。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took Jiqing Road and became Prince of Wu, he abolished the various wing unified-army commanders-in-chief and established seventeen personal-guard command offices: Wude, Longxiang, Baotao, Feixiong, Weiwu, Guangwu, Xingwu, Yingwu, Yingyang, Xiaoqi, Shenwu, Xiongwu, Fengxiang, Tiance, Zhenwu, Xuanwu, and Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founding Emperor secured Jiqing and assumed the title Prince of Wu, he abolished the wing-level unified-army marshals and set up seventeen command offices for his personal guards—Wude, Longxiang, Baotao, Feixiong, Weiwu, Guangwu, Xingwu, Yingwu, Yingyang, Xiaoqi, Shenwu, Xiongwu, Fengxiang, Tiance, Zhenwu, Xuanwu, and Yulin.

sentences.zh: 革諸將襲元舊制樞密、平章、元帥、總管、萬戶諸官號，而核其所部兵五千人為指揮，千人為千戶，百人為百戶，五十人為總旗，十人為小旗。

translations.literal: He abolished the Yuan-era titles the generals had inherited—Privy Councillor, Grand Councillor, Commander-in-Chief, Chief, and Ten-Thousand-Household—and reorganized their troops into units of five thousand as a command, one thousand as a thousand-household, one hundred as a hundred-household, fifty as a chief banner, and ten as a petty banner.
translations.idiomatic: He swept away the Yuan titles the commanders had carried over—Privy Councillor, Grand Councillor, Marshal, Chief, and Ten-Thousand-Household—and restructured their forces into commands of five thousand, thousand-household units of one thousand, hundred-household units of one hundred, chief banners of fifty, and petty banners of ten.

sentences.zh: 天下既定，度要害地，系一郡者設所，連郡者設衛。

translations.literal: After the realm was settled, surveying key terrain, where a single prefecture was involved a post was established; where several prefectures were linked, a guard was established.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empire was secure, the government surveyed strategic ground: a single prefecture received a post, while a cluster of linked prefectures received a guard.

sentences.zh: 大率五千六百人為衛，千一百二十人為千戶所，百十有二人為百戶所。

translations.literal: Generally, five thousand six hundred men formed a guard; one thousand one hundred twenty men formed a thousand-household post; one hundred twelve men formed a hundred-household post.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, a guard mustered about 5,600 men, a thousand-household post about 1,120, and a hundred-household post about 112.

sentences.zh: 所設總旗二，小旗十，大小聯比以成軍。

translations.literal: Each post had two chief banners and ten petty banners, linking large and small units to form the army.
translations.idiomatic: Each post was built from two chief banners and ten petty banners, nesting smaller units within larger ones until the full force took shape.

sentences.zh: 其取兵，有從征，有歸附，有謫發。

translations.literal: Troops were drawn from three sources: campaign followers, surrendered units, and exiled draftees.
translations.idiomatic: Recruits came from three channels: men who had followed campaigns, men who had surrendered, and men drafted through penal exile.

sentences.zh: 從征者，諸將所部兵，既定其地，因以留戍。

translations.literal: Campaign followers were troops under the various generals; once an area was secured, they were left behind as garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign followers were the soldiers under each field commander; when a region was pacified, they were left there to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 歸附，則勝國及僭偽諸降卒。

translations.literal: Surrendered units were troops of the defeated state and various rebel pretenders who had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered troops were soldiers of the fallen dynasty and of the various rebel regimes that had submitted.

sentences.zh: 謫發，以罪遷隸為兵者。

translations.literal: Exiled draftees were those transferred to military service as punishment for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Penal drafts were offenders banished into military registration.

sentences.zh: 其軍皆世籍。

translations.literal: All these armies were hereditary registers.
translations.idiomatic: Every such army was entered on a hereditary military register.

sentences.zh: 此其大略也。

translations.literal: This was the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad design.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，升杭州、江西、燕山、青州四衛為都衛，復置河南、西安、太原、武昌四都衛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, the four guards Hangzhou, Jiangxi, Yanshan, and Qingzhou were promoted to regional guards, and the four regional guards Henan, Xi'an, Taiyuan, and Wuchang were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3, Hangzhou, Jiangxi, Yanshan, and Qingzhou guards were raised to regional-guard status, and the regional guards at Henan, Xi'an, Taiyuan, and Wuchang were restored.

sentences.zh: 四年，造用寶金符及調發走馬符牌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, gold seals for imperial use and dispatch tally plaques for urgent mobilization were made.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, the court cast the imperial gold tally seals and the iron dispatch plaques used to mobilize troops at speed.

sentences.zh: 用寶符為小金牌二，中書省、大都督府各藏其一。

translations.literal: The imperial-use seals were two small gold plates; the Secretariat and the Grand Military Commission each kept one.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tallies were a pair of small gold plates, one held by the Secretariat and one by the Grand Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 有詔發兵，省府以牌入，內府出寶用之。

translations.literal: When there was an imperial order to deploy troops, the ministry or commission would present its plaque; the inner palace would bring out the imperial seal for use.
translations.idiomatic: On an order to mobilize, the responsible ministry or commission submitted its plaque; the inner palace then produced the imperial tally for authentication.

sentences.zh: 走馬符牌，鐵為之，共四十，金字、銀字者各半，藏之內府。

translations.literal: The dispatch tally plaques were of iron, forty in all, half inscribed in gold and half in silver, stored in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The urgent-dispatch plaques were iron—forty in all, half gold-inscribed and half silver-inscribed—kept in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 有急務調發，使者佩以行。

translations.literal: For urgent tasks requiring mobilization, envoys carried them on their missions.
translations.idiomatic: When an emergency mobilization was required, couriers wore them on the road.

sentences.zh: 尋改為金符。

translations.literal: Soon they were changed to gold tally plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Before long these were replaced with gold tallies.

sentences.zh: 凡軍機文書，自都督府、中書省長官外，不許擅奏。

translations.literal: Regarding military documents, aside from the chiefs of the Military Commission and Secretariat, no one was permitted to memorialize on them without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: On military papers, no one below the heads of the Military Commission and Secretariat might memorialize without leave.

sentences.zh: 有詔調軍，省、府同覆奏，然後納符請寶。

translations.literal: When there was an order to mobilize troops, the ministries and commission would jointly review and memorialize, then present the tally and request the imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were to be called out, the ministries and commission reviewed the matter together, memorialized jointly, and only then submitted the tally and requested the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 五年，置親王護衛指揮使司，每府三護衛，衛設左、右、中、前、後五所；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, princely guard command offices were established; each princely estate had three guards; each guard had five posts—left, right, center, front, and rear;
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, command offices for princely guards were created: three guards per princely establishment, each guard divided into left, right, center, front, and rear posts;

sentences.zh: 所，千戶二，百戶十。

translations.literal: each post had two thousand-households and ten hundred-households.
translations.idiomatic: each post with two thousand-household officers and ten hundred-household officers.

sentences.zh: 圍子手所二；

translations.literal: two bowmen posts;
translations.idiomatic: There were also two bowmen posts;

sentences.zh: 所，千戶一。

translations.literal: each with one thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: each with a single thousand-household officer.

sentences.zh: 七年，申定兵衛之政，徵調則統於諸將，事平則散歸各衛。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the policy on guard garrisons was reaffirmed: when mobilized, troops were unified under the generals; when affairs were settled, they dispersed back to their respective guards.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 the guard system was reaffirmed: on campaign, units assembled under field commanders; when peace returned, they dispersed again to their home guards.

sentences.zh: 八年，改在京留守都衛為留守衛指揮使司，在外都衛為都指揮使司，凡十三：北平、陝西、山西、浙江、江西、山東、四川、福建、湖廣、廣東、廣西、遼東、河南。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the capital garrison regional guards were changed to capital garrison guard command offices, and exterior regional guards to regional command offices—thirteen in all: Beiping, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Shandong, Sichuan, Fujian, Huguang, Guangdong, Guangxi, Liaodong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the capital's garrison regional guards became capital garrison command offices, and those in the provinces became regional military commissions—thirteen altogether: Beiping, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Shandong, Sichuan, Fujian, Huguang, Guangdong, Guangxi, Liaodong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 又行都指揮使司二：甘州、大同。

translations.literal: Two mobile regional command offices were also established: Ganzhou and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Two frontier regional commissions were added as well: Ganzhou and Datong.

sentences.zh: 俱隸大都督府。

translations.literal: All were subordinate to the Grand Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: All fell under the Grand Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 九年，選公、侯、都督、各衛指揮嫡長次子為散騎、參侍舍人，隸都督府，充宿衛，或署各衛所事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the legitimate eldest sons of dukes, marquises, regional commanders, and guard commanders were selected as idle cavaliers and attendant retainers, attached to the Military Commission to serve as palace guards or to act in place at various guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the eldest legitimate sons of dukes, marquises, regional commanders, and guard commanders were chosen as palace attendants under the Military Commission, to stand night watch or to deputize at guard posts.

sentences.zh: 十三年，丞相胡惟庸謀反誅，革中書省，因改大都督府為五，分統諸軍司衛所。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Chancellor Hu Weiyong was executed for treason; the Secretariat was abolished, and accordingly the Grand Military Commission was split into five, each controlling various army offices, guards, and posts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 Chancellor Hu Weiyong was put to death for treason, the Secretariat was abolished, and the Grand Military Commission was divided into five commissions, each overseeing its share of army offices, guards, and posts.

sentences.zh: 明年，復置中都留守司及貴州、雲南都指揮使司。

translations.literal: The next year, the Zhongdu garrison office and the Guizhou and Yunnan regional command offices were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Zhongdu garrison office and the Guizhou and Yunnan regional commissions were restored.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，頒軍法定律。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, the military statutes were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 15 the military code was issued.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔各都司上衛所城池水陸地理圖。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict ordered each regional command to submit maps of guard-post fortifications and land and water geography.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 each regional commission was ordered to submit maps of its guard-post walls and of local land and water routes.

sentences.zh: 二十年，置大寧都指揮使司。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the Daning regional command office was established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 the Daning regional commission was established.

sentences.zh: 是年，命兵部置軍籍勘合，載從軍履歷、調補衛所年月、在營丁口之數，給內外衛所軍士，而藏其副於內府。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of War was ordered to prepare military registers and verification documents recording service history, dates of transfer and assignment to guard posts, and household numbers in camp, issued to guard soldiers inside and outside the capital, with duplicates stored in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Ministry of War was told to issue military registers listing each soldier's service record, dates of transfer among posts, and household numbers in camp; copies went to guards throughout the realm, duplicates to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 三十年，定武官役軍之制：指揮、同知、僉事四，千戶三，百戶、鎮撫二，皆取正軍，三日一番上，下直歸伍操練。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the system for military officers serving rotation duty was fixed: commanders, deputy commanders, and assistant commanders four days; thousand-households three; hundred-households and protectors two—all drawn from regular troops, rotating every three days on and off duty, returning to their units for drill when off.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 the rotation duty of officers was fixed: commanders, deputies, and assistants served four days, thousand-household officers three, hundred-household officers and protectors two—all drawn from active soldiers, on duty every third day and drilling with their units when off.

sentences.zh: 衛所直廳六，守門二，守監四，守庫一，皆任老軍，月一更。

translations.literal: Six direct-office duties at guard posts, two gate guards, four prison guards, one arsenal guard—all assigned to veteran soldiers, rotating monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Six headquarters posts, two gate watches, four prison watches, and one storehouse watch at each guard were filled by veteran soldiers on a monthly rotation.

sentences.zh: 建文帝嗣位，置河北都司、湖廣行都司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen succeeded, the Hebei regional office and Huguang mobile regional office were established.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Jianwen's accession, the Hebei regional commission and the Huguang frontier commission were created.

sentences.zh: 文皇入立，皆罷之，而升燕山三護衛為親軍，並建文時所立孝陵衛，皆不隸五府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen (Yongle) took the throne, all were abolished; the three Yanshan princely guards were promoted to personal guards, together with the Xiaoling Guard established under Jianwen—all outside the five commissions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor seized the throne, he abolished them all, elevated the three Yanshan princely guards to personal guards, and likewise exempted the Xiaoling Guard Jianwen had founded—all standing outside the five military commissions.

sentences.zh: 後諸陵設衛皆如之。

translations.literal: Later, whenever tombs had guards established, it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Later imperial tombs that received guards followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 移山西行都司所屬諸衛軍於北平，設衛屯種。

translations.literal: Troops from guards under the Shanxi mobile regional office were moved to Beiping, and guard colonies for farming were set up.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers from the guards under the Shanxi frontier commission were transferred to Beiping, and guard farming colonies were established.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，罷北平都司，設留守行後軍都督府，遷大寧都司於保定。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, the Beiping regional office was abolished, a rear military commissioner's office for the capital garrison was established, and the Daning regional office was moved to Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 the Beiping regional commission was abolished, a rear military commission for the capital garrison was set up, and the Daning commission was moved to Baoding.

sentences.zh: 明年，更定衛所屯守軍士。

translations.literal: The next year, garrison and farming troops at guard posts were redefined.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the division between garrison duty and farming duty at guard posts was redrawn.

sentences.zh: 臨邊險要者，守多於屯。

translations.literal: On critical frontier borders, garrison duty outweighed farming.
translations.idiomatic: On dangerous frontiers, more men stood watch than worked the fields.

sentences.zh: 在內平僻，或地雖險要而運輸難至者，皆屯多於守。

translations.literal: In peaceful interior regions, or where terrain was critical but transport difficult, farming outweighed garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In quiet interior districts, or where the ground was strategic but supplies hard to reach, farming outweighed garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 七年，置調軍勘合，以勇、敢、鋒、銳、神、奇、精、壯、強、毅、克、勝、英、雄、威、猛十六字，編百號。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, troop mobilization tallies were established, using sixteen characters—Brave, Daring, Sharp, Keen, Divine, Strange, Fine, Robust, Strong, Resolute, Conquer, Victor, Hero, Champion, Might, Fierce—to compile a hundred serial numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 mobilization tallies were introduced, built from sixteen characters—Brave, Daring, Sharp, Keen, Divine, Strange, Fine, Robust, Strong, Resolute, Conquer, Victor, Hero, Champion, Might, and Fierce—to form a hundred serial codes.

sentences.zh: 制敕調軍及遣將，比號同，方準行。

translations.literal: Imperial orders to mobilize troops and dispatch generals required matching serial numbers before action was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders to mobilize troops or appoint generals took effect only when the serial numbers matched.

sentences.zh: 十八年，北京建，在南諸衛多北調。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when Beijing was built, many southern guards were transferred north.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, as Beijing was built, many southern guards were shifted north.

sentences.zh: 宣德五，年從平江伯陳瑄言，以衛官職漕運，東南之卒由是困。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande, following the counsel of Chen Xuan, Earl of Pingjiang, guard officers were assigned grain-transport duty; southeastern troops suffered accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xuande reign, on the advice of Chen Xuan, Earl of Pingjiang, guard officers were put in charge of grain transport, and soldiers of the southeast bore the burden.

sentences.zh: 八年，減衛軍餘丁，正軍外每軍留一，餘悉遣歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, surplus household members of guard troops were reduced: aside from the primary soldier one man was kept per household, the rest all sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 surplus males in guard households were cut back: besides the registered soldier, only one man per household was kept; the rest were sent home.

sentences.zh: 已，復以幼軍備操者不足，三丁至七八丁者選一，餘聽治生，給軍裝。

translations.literal: Later, because young soldiers available for drill were insufficient, where three to seven or eight sons existed one was selected; the rest were permitted to pursue livelihoods and were given military gear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because there were not enough young soldiers for drill, households with three to as many as seven or eight sons chose one; the others were allowed to make their living elsewhere and were issued kit.

sentences.zh: 正軍有故，即令補伍，毋再勾攝。

translations.literal: When the primary soldier had cause (death, etc.), he was immediately replaced in the unit; no second conscription.
translations.idiomatic: When the registered soldier died or was removed, a replacement filled the slot at once without a fresh levy.

sentences.zh: 當是時，都指揮使與布、按並稱三司，為封疆大吏。

translations.literal: At that time, regional commanders were ranked with provincial administration and surveillance commissioners as the 'Three Offices,' great officials of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In that era the regional commander stood with the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners as one of the 'Three Offices'—a great officer of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 而專閫重臣，文武亦無定職，世猶以武為重，軍政修飭。

translations.literal: Yet frontier commanders with heavy responsibility had no fixed civil or military role; the age still valued martial affairs, and military government was well regulated.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanders with full powers had no fixed civil or military title, yet society still esteemed the martial arts and military administration remained tight.

sentences.zh: 正德以來，軍職冒濫，為世所輕。

translations.literal: Since the Zhengde reign, military posts were corruptly inflated and held in contempt by society.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhengde reign onward, military offices were bought and padded until the world held them cheap.

sentences.zh: 內之部科，外之監軍、督撫，疊相彈壓，五軍府如贅疣，弁帥如走卒。

translations.literal: Within, ministry sections; without, military supervisors, governors-general, and surveillance commissioners—layer upon layer of pressure; the Five Military Commissions were like useless appendages, commanders like running dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, ministry sections; outside, army supervisors, governors-general, and grand coordinators—each layer pressing down on the next; the Five Commissions became dead weight, and field officers little better than runners.

sentences.zh: 總兵官領敕於兵部，皆跽，間為長揖，即謂非禮。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-chief receiving edicts from the Ministry of War all knelt; occasionally offering a long bow was considered improper.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders receiving orders from the Ministry of War knelt to take them; even a formal bow was sometimes judged disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 至於末季，衛所軍士，雖一諸生可役使之。

translations.literal: By the final years, guard soldiers could be ordered about by a mere licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: By the dynasty's end, a mere student could order guard soldiers about.

sentences.zh: 積輕積弱，重以隱佔、虛冒諸弊，至舉天下之兵，不足以任戰守，而明遂亡矣。

translations.literal: Accumulated lightness and weakness, compounded by abuses of concealed registration and false claims, until the empire's troops could not bear defense or battle—and the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: Neglect and weakness piled up, together with hidden registers and false rolls, until the empire's armies could neither fight nor hold the line—and the Ming fell.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，範景文以兵部侍郎守通州，上言：「祖制，邊腹內外，衛所棋置，以軍隸衛，以屯養軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen, Fan Jingwen, as Vice Minister of War defending Tongzhou, memorialized: 'Under the ancestral system, frontier, interior, inner and outer, guard posts were set like chess pieces—armies subordinated to guards, colonies sustaining armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 3, Fan Jingwen, vice minister of war while holding Tongzhou, wrote: 'Under the ancestral design, guards and posts were laid out like chess pieces across border and interior, inner realm and outer—soldiers belonged to guards, and farming colonies fed the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 後失其制，軍外募民為兵，屯外賦民出餉，使如鱗尺籍，不能為衝鋒之事，並不知帶甲之人。

translations.literal: Later the system was lost: outside the army, civilians were recruited as soldiers; outside colonies, civilians were taxed for grain—making registers like fish scales, unable to charge in battle, not knowing who wore armor.
translations.idiomatic: Later the system broke down: beyond the old army, civilians were hired as troops; beyond the colonies, civilians paid rations—registers grew like fish scales, yet men could not charge in battle and no one knew who actually wore armor.

sentences.zh: 陛下百度振刷，豈可令有定之軍數付之不可問，有用之軍糈投之不可知？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has refreshed a hundred policies—how can fixed troop numbers be handed to the unaccountable, and useful military grain cast to the unknown?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is renewing every policy—how can fixed troop totals be left unaccounted for, and useful military grain poured into channels no one can trace?

sentences.zh: 因條上清核數事，不果行。

translations.literal: He then listed several items for clearing and verification, but they were not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted several proposals for auditing the rolls, but none was carried out.

sentences.zh: 初，洪武二十六年定天下都司衛所，共計都司十有七，留守司一，內外衛三百二十九，守禦千戶所六十五。

translations.literal: Initially, in the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu the empire's regional offices, guards, and posts were fixed: seventeen regional offices, one garrison office, 329 interior and exterior guards, 65 defensive thousand-household posts.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in Hongwu year 26 the realm's commissions, guards, and posts were tallied: seventeen regional commissions, one garrison office, 329 guards inside and outside the capital, and 65 defensive thousand-household posts.

sentences.zh: 及成祖在位二十餘年，多所增改。

translations.literal: During the more than twenty years of Chengzu's reign, many additions and changes were made.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle Emperor's more than twenty years on the throne, many were added or altered.

sentences.zh: 其後措置不一，今區別其名於左，以資考鏡。

translations.literal: Later arrangements were inconsistent; their names are distinguished below for reference.

sentences.zh: 自是番僧有封灌頂國師及贊善、闡化等王，大乘大寶法王者，俱給印誥，傳以為信。

translations.literal: Thereafter Tibetan monks received enfeoffment as consecration national preceptors and as kings of Goodness, Propagation, and the like, and as Mahayana Great Treasure Dharma Kings—all given patent letters and seals handed down as credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tibetan monks were enfeoffed as consecration national preceptors and as Goodness, Propagation, and Mahayana Great Treasure dharma kings, each with patent letters and seals as credentials.

translations.idiomatic: Rotational troops are guard and post soldiers who rotate to the capital for duty, forming the three great camps.

sentences.zh: 初，永樂十三年詔邊將及河南、山東、山西、陝西各都司，中都留守司，江南、北諸衛官，簡所部卒赴北京，以俟臨閱。

translations.literal: Initially, in the thirteenth year of Yongle, an edict ordered frontier generals and the regional commands of Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, and Shaanxi, the Central Capital garrison command, and officers of guards south and north of the Yangtze to select troops from their commands to proceed to Beijing to await inspection.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, in Yongle year 13, the throne ordered frontier generals and the Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, and Shaanxi regional commands, the Central Capital garrison command, and guard officers north and south of the Yangtze to pick men from their units for Beijing, there to await review.

sentences.zh: 京操自此始。

translations.literal: Capital drill began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Capital drill dates from this measure.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，因英國公張輔等言，調直隸及近京軍番上操備，諭以畢農而來，先農務遣歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renzong reign, on the words of Zhang Fu, Duke of Yingguo, and others, troops of Zhili and guards near the capital were rotated to drill in reserve; they were instructed to come after finishing farm work, and when farm work took priority they were sent home first.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renzong reign, on the advice of Zhang Fu, Duke of Yingguo, and others, Zhili and near-capital troops were put on rotating drill duty, told to report only after the harvest, and sent home whenever farm work came first.

sentences.zh: 既而輔言：「邊軍比悉放還，京軍少，請調山東、河南、中都、淮、揚諸衛校閱。」

translations.literal: Later Fu said: "Frontier troops have nearly all been sent home; capital troops are few. Request that guards of Shandong, Henan, the Central Capital, Huai, and Yang be transferred for review."
translations.idiomatic: Fu soon added: "Frontier troops have almost all been released; the capital is short of men. I ask that guards in Shandong, Henan, the Central Capital, Huai, and Yang be called up for inspection.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可」。

translations.literal: The rescript said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 又敕河南、山東、山西、大寧及中都將領，凡軍還取衣裝者，以三月畢務，七月至京，老弱者選代，官給之馬。

translations.literal: Another edict instructed generals of Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, Daning, and the Central Capital: for troops returning to fetch kit, farm work must be finished by the third month; they must reach the capital by the seventh month; the aged and weak were to be replaced by selection, and the state provided horses.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict told the Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, Daning, and Central Capital commanders that troops sent home for kit must finish farm work by the third month and reach Beijing by the seventh; the old and weak were to be replaced by selection, with official horses supplied.

sentences.zh: 歲春秋番上，共十六萬人：大寧七萬七百餘，中都、山東遞殺，河南最少，僅一萬四千有奇。

translations.literal: Each year they rotated to the capital in spring and autumn, totaling 160,000 men: Daning 70,700-odd, decreasing in turn from the Central Capital and Shandong; Henan the fewest, barely over 14,000.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn rotations brought 160,000 men to the capital each year: Daning supplied more than 70,700; the Central Capital and Shandong contributed less in turn; Henan the least, barely 14,000-odd.

sentences.zh: 定為例。

translations.literal: This was fixed as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This became fixed precedent.

sentences.zh: 後允成國公硃勇等請，罷鞏昌諸衛及階、文千戶所班軍，代以陝西內地卒。

translations.literal: Later, on the request of Zhu Yong, Duke of Chengguo, and others, guards at Gongchang and thousand-household posts at Jie and Wen were removed from rotational duty and replaced with troops from inland Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the request of Zhu Yong, Duke of Chengguo, and others, Gongchang guards and the Jie and Wen thousand-household posts were dropped from rotation and replaced with inland Shaanxi troops.

sentences.zh: 山東衛士沿海備倭，沿海衛士復內調，通州衛士漕淮安粟，安慶衛士赴京操，不便，皆更之。

translations.literal: Shandong guard soldiers guarding the coast against wokou, coastal guard soldiers transferred inland, Tongzhou guard soldiers hauling Huai'an grain, and Anqing guard soldiers coming to the capital for drill were all inconvenient and were all changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong guards posted on the coast against wokou, coastal guards pulled inland, Tongzhou guards hauling Huai'an grain, and Anqing guards drilling at the capital were all awkward arrangements and were all revised.

sentences.zh: 已，並放還陝西班軍。

translations.literal: Later, Shaanxi rotational troops were also all sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi rotational troops were soon sent home as well.

sentences.zh: 正統中，京操軍皆戍邊，乃遣御史於江北、山東、北直選卒，為京師備。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign, all capital-drill troops were on frontier garrison duty, so censors were sent to north of the Yangtze, Shandong, and Beizhili to select troops as capital reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengtong, capital-drill troops were all on frontier duty, so censors were dispatched to Jiangbei, Shandong, and Beizhili to levy men as a capital reserve.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，邊事棘，班軍悉留京，間歲乃放還取衣裝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, frontier affairs were urgent; all rotational troops were kept at the capital, and every other year they were sent home to fetch kit.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingtai began his reign, frontier alarms were acute; rotational troops were all kept in Beijing and sent home for kit only every other year.

sentences.zh: 於是于謙、石亨議三分之，留兩番操備。

translations.literal: Yu Qian and Shi Heng then proposed dividing them into thirds, keeping two rotations for drill reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian and Shi Heng then proposed splitting the force in three, keeping two rotations on drill duty in the capital.

sentences.zh: 保定、河間、天津放五十日，河南、山東九十日，淮、揚、中都百日，紫荊、倒馬、白羊三關及保定諸城戍卒，屬山東、河南者，亦如之。

translations.literal: Baoding, Hejian, and Tianjin received fifty days' leave; Henan and Shandong ninety days; Huai, Yang, and the Central Capital one hundred days; garrison troops at Zijing, Daoma, and Baiyang passes and walled cities of Baoding subordinate to Shandong and Henan had the same.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding, Hejian, and Tianjin troops received fifty days' leave; Henan and Shandong ninety; Huai, Yang, and the Central Capital one hundred; garrison men at Zijing, Daoma, and Baiyang passes and Baoding's walled cities under Shandong or Henan were treated the same.

sentences.zh: 逃者，官鐫秩三等，卒盡室謫邊衛。

translations.literal: Deserters had their ranks reduced three grades; soldiers and entire families were banished to frontier guards.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters cost their officers three ranks; soldiers and whole households were banished to frontier guards.

sentences.zh: 明年，謙又言：「班軍分十營團練，久不得休，請仍分兩番。」

translations.literal: The next year Qian again said: "Rotational troops are divided into ten camps for mass training and long without rest. Request they be divided into two rotations again."
translations.idiomatic: The next year Qian urged again: "Rotational troops are massed in ten camps and long without rest. Let them rotate in two batches again.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Reply: approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 成化間，河南秋班軍二千餘不至，下御史趣之。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign, more than 2,000 autumn-rotation troops from Henan failed to arrive; censors were sent to hurry them.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua, more than 2,000 Henan autumn-rotation troops failed to appear; censors were sent to hurry them along.

sentences.zh: 海內燕安，外衛卒在京只供營繕諸役，勢家私佔復半之。

translations.literal: Within the realm there was ease; outer-guard troops at the capital only supplied labor for construction and the like, and powerful families privately occupied half of them again.
translations.idiomatic: With peace inside the realm, outer-guard men in the capital served only on construction and the like, while powerful households privately claimed half of them again.

sentences.zh: 卒多畏苦，往往愆期，乃定遠限罪，輕者發居庸、密雲、山海關罰班六月。

translations.literal: Troops mostly feared hardship and often missed deadlines; limits on lateness and penalties were then fixed—the lightest sent to Juyong, Miyun, and Shanhai passes for six months' penalty rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers mostly dreaded the hardship and often arrived late, so deadlines and penalties were set: lighter cases were sent to Juyong, Miyun, and Shanhai passes for six months' penalty rotation.

sentences.zh: 重者發邊衛罰班至年半。

translations.literal: The severe were sent to frontier guards for penalty rotation up to a year and a half.
translations.idiomatic: Severe cases were posted to frontier guards for penalty rotation of up to eighteen months.

sentences.zh: 令雖具，然不能革也。

translations.literal: Though the orders were complete, they could not be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: The rules were on the books, yet the abuse could not be uprooted.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，兵部言佔役之害，罰治如議。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign the Ministry of War reported harm from private requisitioning; penalties were enforced as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi the Ministry of War reported the harm of private requisitioning, and penalties were applied as proposed.

sentences.zh: 於是選衛兵八萬團操，內外各半。

translations.literal: Then 80,000 guard soldiers were selected for mass drill, half within and half without the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty thousand guard troops were then chosen for mass drill, half from the capital districts and half from outer guards.

sentences.zh: 外衛四萬，兩番迭上。

translations.literal: Outer guards 40,000, rotating in two batches.
translations.idiomatic: Outer guards supplied 40,000 men, rotating in two batches.

sentences.zh: 李東陽極言工作困軍，班軍逾期不至，大率坐此。

translations.literal: Li Dongyang strongly stated that construction work exhausted troops and rotational troops often failed to arrive on time—mostly for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang argued forcefully that construction work broke the troops and that rotational troops usually arrived late—chiefly for this reason.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 末年，歸大寧卒兩班萬人。

translations.literal: In his last years, two rotations of Daning troops totaling 10,000 men were returned.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years, two Daning rotations totaling 10,000 men were sent home.

sentences.zh: 正德中，宣府軍及京營互調，春秋番換如班軍例。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign, Xuanfu troops and capital-camp troops were mutually transferred, spring and autumn rotation like rotational troops precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, Xuanfu and capital-camp troops were exchanged in spring and autumn rotations on the rotational-troop model.

sentences.zh: 迄世宗立乃已。

translations.literal: This continued until the Shizong emperor took the throne and then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The practice lasted until the Jiajing emperor's accession, when it stopped.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，尚書李承勳言：「永樂中調軍番上京師，後遂踵為故事，衛伍半空，而在京者徒供營造。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing, Minister Li Chengxun said: "In Yongle troops were transferred to rotate at the capital; later it became precedent; guard ranks were half empty while those at the capital merely supplied construction.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing, Minister Li Chengxun said: "Under Yongle, troops were rotated to the capital; the practice hardened into precedent, leaving guard rolls half empty while men in Beijing did nothing but construction.

sentences.zh: 不若省行糧之費，以募工作。」

translations.literal: Better to save travel-grain costs and hire labor for works.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to save travel grain and hire labor for public works.

sentences.zh: 御史鮑象賢請分班軍為三，二入營操，一以赴役。

translations.literal: Censor Bao Xiangxian requested dividing rotational troops into three—two entering camps for drill, one for labor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Bao Xiangxian asked to split rotational troops three ways: two parts to drill in camp, one to labor.

sentences.zh: 通政司陳經復請半放之，收其糧募工。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Jing again requested sending half home and collecting their grain to hire workers.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Jing again proposed releasing half and using their grain rations to hire workers.

sentences.zh: 皆不行。

translations.literal: None were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: None of these plans was adopted.

sentences.zh: 久之，從翊國公郭勳言，寬河南因災不至班軍，而諭後犯者罪必如法。

translations.literal: After long time, on Guo Xun, Duke of Yiguo's, advice, Henan rotational troops who failed to arrive owing to disaster were excused, while those violating thereafter were to be punished strictly by law.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, on the advice of Guo Xun, Duke of Yiguo, Henan rotational troops delayed by disaster were excused, while later offenders were warned that the law would be enforced without leniency.

sentences.zh: 兵部因條議，軍士失期，治將領之罪，以多寡為差，重者至鐫秩戍邊。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War thereupon itemized regulations: when soldiers missed deadlines, commanders were punished in proportion to numbers—the severe even reduced in rank and garrisoned on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War then laid down rules: when soldiers missed rotation, commanders were punished in proportion to the numbers involved, the heaviest cases costing rank and frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Reply: approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 其後邊警棘，乃並番上軍為一班，五月赴京，十一月放還，每歲秋防見兵十五六萬。

translations.literal: Later frontier alarms were urgent; troops on rotation were merged into one batch—arriving at capital in fifth month, released in eleventh month; each year autumn defense had 150,000–160,000 troops on hand.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier alarms grew acute, rotating troops were merged into a single batch arriving in the fifth month and released in the eleventh; each autumn the capital could field 150,000 to 160,000 men.

sentences.zh: 仇鸞用事，抽邊卒入衛，凡選士六萬八千餘。

translations.literal: Qiu Luan wielded power and drew frontier troops into guards; in all over 68,000 men were selected.
translations.idiomatic: While Qiu Luan held power, he drew frontier soldiers into capital guards, selecting more than 68,000 men in all.

sentences.zh: 又免大寧等衛軍京操，改防薊鎮，班軍遂耗減。

translations.literal: Also exempted Daning and other guards from capital drill, changed them to garrison Ji garrison; rotational troops thus dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Daning and other guards were also exempted from capital drill and reassigned to the Ji garrison, and rotational numbers shrank.

sentences.zh: 豐城侯李熙核其數，僅四萬人，因請改徵銀召募，而以見軍四萬歸營操練。

translations.literal: Li Xi, Marquis of Fengcheng, audited the count—only 40,000 men—and requested replacing levy with silver for recruitment while the 40,000 on hand returned to camp drill.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, Marquis of Fengcheng, audited the rolls and found only 40,000 men; he asked to levy silver for recruitment and put the 40,000 present troops back under camp drill.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩議以「各衛兵雖有折幹之弊，然清核令下，猶凜凜畏罪。

translations.literal: Yan Song argued: "Though each guard's troops had the ill of zhegan, when the clear audit order was issued they still feared punishment keenly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song argued: "Although every guard suffered from the zhegan abuse, once the audit order went out the men still feared punishment.

sentences.zh: 若奉旨徵銀，恐借為口實，祖宗良法深意，一旦蕩然」。

translations.literal: If silver collection were by imperial edict, one fears it would become a pretext; the deep intent of the ancestral good method would at once be swept away."
translations.idiomatic: If the throne ordered silver collection in place of service, people would seize on it as a pretext and the ancestral system would collapse overnight."

sentences.zh: 帝是之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 折幹者，衛卒納銀，將弁以免其行，有事則召募以應。

translations.literal: Zhegan meant guard soldiers paid silver and officers avoided their going; when there was business recruits were raised to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhegan meant guard soldiers paid silver so officers could excuse them from rotation; when need arose, recruits were hired to fill the gap.

sentences.zh: 亡何，從平江伯陳圭奏，仍令中都、山東、河南軍分春秋兩班，別為一營，春以三月至，八月還，秋以九月至，來歲二月還，工作毋擅役。

translations.literal: Before long, on Chen Gui, Earl of Pingjiang's, memorial, Central Capital, Shandong, and Henan troops were again divided into spring and autumn two batches in a separate camp—spring arriving third month returning eighth month; autumn arriving ninth month returning second month next year; work must not be requisitioned without authority.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on Chen Gui, Earl of Pingjiang's, memorial, Central Capital, Shandong, and Henan troops were again split into spring and autumn batches in a separate camp: spring troops arrived in the third month and left in the eighth; autumn troops arrived in the ninth and left the following second month; labor could not be assigned without authorization.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，大發治河，軍人憚久役，逃亡多。

translations.literal: Early Longqing, great river works were launched; soldiers feared long service and deserted in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing, major river works were launched; soldiers dreaded long service and deserted in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 部議於見役軍中，簡銳者著伍，而以老弱供畚鍤。

translations.literal: The ministry proposed among troops on active duty selecting sharp men for ranks while old and weak supplied shovels and baskets.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry proposed picking the able-bodied for combat ranks among troops on active duty and assigning the old and weak to shovel and basket work.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，科臣言，班軍非為工作設。

translations.literal: Wanli year 2, a supervising secretary said rotational troops were not established for labor.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 2, a supervising secretary said rotational troops were not created to serve as laborers.

sentences.zh: 下兵部，止議以小工不得概派而已。

translations.literal: Referred to Ministry of War—they only discussed that small works must not be assigned wholesale.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the Ministry of War, which would only say that minor jobs must not be assigned wholesale.

sentences.zh: 時積弊已久，軍士苦役甚，多愆期不至。

translations.literal: By then abuses were long-standing; soldiers suffered labor severely and many missed deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: By then abuses were entrenched; soldiers were crushed by labor and many failed to arrive on time.

sentences.zh: 故事，失班脫逃者，罰工銀，追月糈。

translations.literal: Precedent: those missing rotation or deserting were fined work silver and monthly grain was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, men who missed rotation or deserted paid a work fine and forfeited monthly grain.

sentences.zh: 其後額外多徵，軍益逃，中都尤甚。

translations.literal: Later extra levies increased; troops deserted more—the Central Capital especially.
translations.idiomatic: Later extra levies multiplied; desertions increased, above all in the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 自嘉靖四十三年後，積逋工銀至五十餘萬兩。

translations.literal: From after Jiajing year 43, accumulated arrears of work silver reached over 500,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiajing year 43, unpaid work fines piled up to more than 500,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 巡撫都御史張翀乞蠲額外工價，軍三犯者，不必罰工，竟調邊衛。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Zhang Chong begged to cancel extra work price; troops offending three times need not be fined for work but were directly transferred to frontier guards.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Chong asked to abolish extra work charges; after three offenses soldiers need not pay work fines but were posted straight to frontier guards.

sentences.zh: 而巡視京營給事中王道成則言：「凡軍一班不到，即系一年脫伍，盡扣月糧。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wang Daocheng inspecting the capital camps said: "Whenever a soldier missed one rotation, it counted as a year's absence from rank and all monthly grain was withheld.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daocheng, supervising secretary inspecting the capital camps, said: "If a soldier missed one rotation, he was counted absent from the rolls for a year and all monthly grain was withheld.

sentences.zh: 本軍仍如例解京，罰補正班。

translations.literal: The original guard still sent replacements to the capital per precedent to make up the regular rotation as penalty.
translations.idiomatic: His home guard still had to send a replacement to the capital as usual to cover the regular rotation as a penalty.

sentences.zh: 三年脫班，仍調邊衛。」

translations.literal: Three years' missing rotation—still transferred to frontier guards."
translations.idiomatic: After three years of missed rotation, he was still transferred to a frontier guard.

sentences.zh: 並報可。

translations.literal: All approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 衛軍益大困。

translations.literal: Guard soldiers were all the more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Guard soldiers were driven still deeper into hardship.

sentences.zh: 後二十九年，帝以班軍多老弱僱倩，令嚴飭之。

translations.literal: Twenty-nine years later, the emperor because many rotational troops were old and weak hired substitutes, ordered strict correction.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine years later, seeing that many rotational troops were old, weak, or hired substitutes, the emperor ordered strict correction.

sentences.zh: 職方主事沈朝煥給班軍餉，皆傭諸丐，因言：「班軍本處有大糧，到京有行糧，又有鹽斤銀，所費十餘萬金，今皆虛冒。

translations.literal: Bureau director Shen Chaohuan distributing rotational rations—all hired from beggars—and said: "Rotational troops at home have large grain; at capital travel grain; also salt-jin silver—cost over 100,000 taels gold; now all falsely claimed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chaohuan of the Bureau of Appointments, issuing rotational pay, found that beggars had been hired in place of soldiers. He said: "Rotational troops draw large grain at home, travel grain in the capital, and salt-jin silver besides—more than 100,000 taels in all—and the claims are largely false.

sentences.zh: 請解大糧貯庫，有警可召募，有工可僱役。」

translations.literal: Request deposit large grain in treasury; when alarm can recruit; for works can hire labor.
translations.idiomatic: Let the large grain be deposited in the treasury: in alarm, recruit; for works, hire labor.

sentences.zh: 部議請先申飭，俟大工竣行之。

translations.literal: Ministry discussed: first urge correction, after major works finish implement.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry replied that discipline should be tightened first and the plan carried out after major works ended.

sentences.zh: 是時專以班軍為役夫，番上之初意盡失矣。

translations.literal: By then rotational troops were used solely as laborers—the original intent of rotation was wholly lost.
translations.idiomatic: By then rotational troops served only as laborers, and the original purpose of rotation was wholly lost.

sentences.zh: 又五年，內庭有小營繕，中官陳永壽請仍用班軍，可節省。

translations.literal: Five years later, minor palace repairs; eunuch Chen Yongshou asked again to use rotational troops, saying it could save expense.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later, when the inner palace needed minor repairs, the eunuch Chen Yongshou again asked to use rotational troops, claiming it would save money.

sentences.zh: 給事中宋一韓爭之，謂：「班軍輸操即三大營軍，所繫甚重。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Song Yihan contested: "Rotational troops sent to drill are the troops of the three great camps—the matter is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Song Yihan objected: "Rotational troops sent up for drill are the backbone of the three great camps—a matter of the highest weight.

sentences.zh: 今邊鄙多事，萬一關吏不謹，而京師團練之軍多召募，遊徼之役多役佔，皇城宿衛多白徒，四衛扈從多廝役。

translations.literal: Now the frontier has many affairs; if perchance pass officers are not careful, capital mass-drill troops largely recruited, patrol duties largely occupied by labor, palace guard largely commoners, four guards escort largely servants.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier is unsettled; if pass officers grow careless, capital drill troops will be mostly recruits, patrol duties mostly seized for labor, palace guards mostly untrained men, and the four escort guards mostly servants.

sentences.zh: 即得三都司健卒三萬，猶不能無恐，況動以興作朘削，名存實亡，緩急何賴哉？」

translations.literal: Even with 30,000 fit troops from the three capital-area commands, one still could not be without fear—how much less when constantly pared by construction; name existing, substance gone—what to rely on in urgency?
translations.idiomatic: Even 30,000 fit men from the three capital-area commands would leave cause for fear—how much less when construction constantly pares them away, leaving the name but not the substance? What would we rely on in an emergency?

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: Not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not listen.

sentences.zh: 四十年，給事中麻僖請恤班操之苦。

translations.literal: Year 40, supervising secretary Ma Xi requested relief for rotational-drill hardship.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40, Supervising Secretary Ma Xi asked relief for the hardships of rotational drill.

sentences.zh: 後六年，順天巡撫都御史劉曰梧言班軍無濟實用，因陳募兵十利。

translations.literal: Six years later, Shuntian grand coordinator Liu Yuewu said rotational troops were of no practical use and set forth ten benefits of recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later, Shuntian Grand Coordinator Liu Yuewu said rotational troops were useless in practice and listed ten advantages of recruitment.

sentences.zh: 是時，法益弛，軍不營操，皆居京師為商販、工藝，以錢入班將。

translations.literal: By then the law was laxer still; soldiers did not drill—all dwelt at capital as merchants and craftsmen, paying silver to rotation officers.
translations.idiomatic: By then discipline had slackened further: soldiers no longer drilled but lived in the capital as traders and artisans, paying silver to their rotation officers.

sentences.zh: 啟、禎時，邊事洶洶，乃移班軍於邊。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen and Taichang times frontier affairs surged; rotational troops were shifted to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen and Taichang, as frontier crises mounted, rotational troops were shifted to the border.

sentences.zh: 築垣、負米無休期，而糗糧缺，軍多死，班將往往逮革。

translations.literal: Building walls and carrying rice without end; grain lacked; many soldiers died; rotation officers were often arrested and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: They built walls and hauled grain without respite; rations ran short; many died; rotation officers were often arrested and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 特敕兵部右侍郎專督理，鑄印給之，然已無及。

translations.literal: Special edict to the Vice Minister of War to supervise exclusively; a seal was cast and given—but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict named a vice minister of war to supervise the matter exclusively and had a seal cast for him—but it was already too late.
